name: Vasily Alekseyev
evidence_summary: Alekseyev's early advantage was primarily physical: the son of a lumberjack in rural Russia, he developed extraordinary strength from childhood physical labor. He started weightlifting relatively late (18) but progressed rapidly through the Soviet sports system, training under Rudolf Plyukfelder from 1966. His exceptional concentration intensity was noted (training three hours without leaving the barbell). By 26, he was the third-best weightlifter in the USSR. No family financial platform or inherited networks are documented; his advantages were physical talent and the Soviet institutional sports pipeline.
early_history_summary: The son of a lumberjack, Alekseyev began weightlifting at age 18 in 1961 while enrolled at the Archangelsk Forestry Institute. He trained under coach Rudolf Plyukfelder after moving to Shakhty in 1966, and by 1967 had joined the 'Club 500' (clean and jerk over 500 kg total). His bronze at the 1968 USSR Championships marked him as a rising talent before his historic dominance beginning in 1970.
family_context_summary: Born in Pokrovo-Shishkino, Ryazan Oblast, the son of a lumberjack. At age 12 he was felling trees and lifting logs for exercise, and at 14 was wrestling woodsmen. He was already 1.8m tall and 90 kg when he enrolled at the Archangelsk Forestry Institute at 18.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a lumberjack; no weightlifting or athletic family background is documented. The rural, physically demanding environment contributed to his natural strength development.
milestone_by_age_26: Won a bronze medal at the 1968 USSR Weightlifting Championships at age 26, placing third in the Soviet Union (the world's dominant weightlifting nation) behind only Leonid Zhabotinsky and Stanislav Batishchev.
primary_early_advantage_tags: lumberjack-son,natural-physical-size,soviet-weightlifting-system,plyukfelder-coaching,intense-self-training,rural-physical-labor

name: Joe Simpson
evidence_summary: Simpson was introduced to climbing at age 14 by a teacher at Ampleforth College and was inspired by The White Spider. By 25, he was an experienced alpine climber who, with partner Simon Yates, completed the first ascent of the west face of Siula Grande in Peru. The high-trust climbing partnership with Yates and years of alpine experience were critical to the achievement. The survival story from this climb became the bestseller Touching the Void.
early_history_summary: Simpson was born in Kuala Lumpur to a Scottish father in the British Army and an Irish mother, and traveled between schools in Britain and various countries. He began rock climbing at age 14 after being introduced to the sport by a teacher at Ampleforth College, and was inspired by Heinrich Harrer's The White Spider. By his mid-twenties he was an experienced alpine climber attempting major first ascents in the Andes.
family_context_summary: Born in Kuala Lumpur to a Scottish father stationed with the British Army and an Irish mother; traveled between schools in Britain and countries where his father was posted. Attended Ampleforth College, a boarding school in Yorkshire.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a British Army officer; no documented mountaineering background in the family. A teacher at Ampleforth College introduced Simpson to climbing.
milestone_by_age_26: Made the first ascent of the previously unclimbed west face of Siula Grande (6,344 m) in the Cordillera Huayhuash of Peru in 1985 at age 25, a major mountaineering achievement that became legendary after his survival story was published in Touching the Void.
primary_early_advantage_tags: boarding school climbing intro, climbing partner Simon Yates, alpine experience, British mountaineering tradition

name: Ai Weiwei
evidence_summary: Ai Weiwei grew up in extreme adversity due to his father's political exile, spending his formative years in labor camps and remote Xinjiang with no access to formal art education. After the Cultural Revolution ended, he enrolled in the Beijing Film Academy at 21 and co-founded the Stars art group, whose 1979 exhibition was shut down by police. His father's literary legacy provided intellectual capital but no material advantage. The post-Cultural Revolution cultural opening was a structural wave, and the Stars collective provided a peer network. His early career was shaped by constraint-driven self-creation rather than inherited advantage.
early_history_summary: Born in Beijing, Ai grew up in exile due to his father Ai Qing's political persecution, spending 16 years in labor camps and remote Xinjiang. After the Cultural Revolution ended, he enrolled in the Beijing Film Academy in 1978 and co-founded the Stars art group, which held an unofficial exhibition in 1979 that was shut down by authorities, making it a seminal moment in Chinese contemporary art.
family_context_summary: Born in Beijing; son of renowned poet Ai Qing, who was denounced during the Anti-Rightist Movement; family was sent to labor camps and exiled to Xinjiang for 16 years, living in harsh conditions.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Ai Qing was a celebrated Chinese poet whose literary prominence and subsequent political persecution profoundly shaped Ai's intellectual environment and political consciousness from childhood.
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded the Stars (Xingxing), an avant-garde art group, in 1978-1979 at age 21-22, and participated in the landmark 1979 Stars exhibition in Beijing that was shut down by police, a defining event in Chinese contemporary art history.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father poet exile, labor camp childhood, Stars art group, post-Cultural Revolution wave, political adversity, Beijing Film Academy

name: Alexis Argüello
evidence_summary: Argüello rose from extreme poverty in Managua, turning professional at 16 after a brief amateur career (58-2). His father was a shoemaker and the family lived in one of Managua's worst neighborhoods. He was trained by Miguel Angel Rivas and overcame early losses to win 29 of 30 bouts, earning a world title shot at 22. His unusual height and reach for a featherweight gave him natural physical advantages. The adversity of his upbringing created the urgency that drove his boxing career.
early_history_summary: Argüello grew up in abject poverty in Managua, Nicaragua, where his father was a shoemaker. He left school at 12, worked on a dairy farm at 9, and spent a year in Canada at 13 to support his family. He compiled a 58-2 amateur record before turning professional at 16 in 1968, and won 29 of his next 30 bouts to earn a world title shot.
family_context_summary: Born into abject poverty in Managua; father was a shoemaker who attempted suicide when Alexis was 5. One of eight children. Left school at 12 and worked to support the family.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family boxing background; Argüello took up boxing after his sister married a boxer. His father was a shoemaker.
milestone_by_age_26: Won the WBA featherweight world championship on November 23, 1974 at age 22 by knocking out Ruben Olivares in the 13th round in Los Angeles.
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty, early pro debut at 16, amateur record 58-2, trainer Miguel Angel Rivas, physical talent

name: Alfonso Zamora
evidence_summary: Zamora grew up in a tough Tlaltelolco neighborhood in Mexico City, falling into drugs and juvenile delinquency before his taxi-driver father took him to a local boxing gym. He won an Olympic silver medal at 18 (1972 Munich), turned professional in 1973, and knocked out Soo-Hwan Hong to win the WBA Bantamweight title at 21 (March 1975). He defended the title five times, including a notable KO of future hall-of-famer Eusebio Pedroza. His background is a classic adversity-catalyst story where boxing provided escape from crime and drugs.
early_history_summary: Zamora grew up in a tough neighborhood in Tlaltelolco, Mexico City, where he fell into drugs and gang life as a child. His father, a taxi driver, took him to a local boxing gym where a coach began his amateur career. He won a silver medal at the 1972 Munich Olympics at 18, turned pro in 1973, and won the WBA Bantamweight title in 1975 at age 21.
family_context_summary: Born in Tlaltelolco, Mexico City to a taxi driver father and a mother who worked; parents had 10 children and could not devote much attention to him. He grew up surrounded by drugs and crime, falling into juvenile delinquency before boxing provided a path out.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family involvement in boxing or sports; father was a taxi driver who directed young Alfonso to a local gym to keep him out of trouble.
milestone_by_age_26: Won a silver medal in bantamweight boxing at the 1972 Munich Olympics at age 18, then became WBA Bantamweight world champion at age 21 in March 1975.
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty and crime catalyst, gym access, Olympic pipeline, Mexican boxing tradition

name: Alfred Brendel
evidence_summary: Brendel's early career was remarkably self-driven: born to a non-musical family with no inherited musical advantages, he was largely self-taught after age 16. His early milestones—the Busoni Competition prize at 18, first recording at 19, and world premiere recording at 21—were achieved through intense self-directed study and concentration. The Graz Conservatory provided foundational training, and master classes with Edwin Fischer offered crucial mentorship. WWII disrupted his childhood, sending him to dig trenches at 14, which may have contributed to his independent, self-reliant approach.
early_history_summary: Brendel was born in Vizmberk, Czechoslovakia, to a non-musical family. He moved to Zagreb at age three and began piano lessons at six with Sofija Deželić. The family later moved to Graz, Austria, where he studied at the Graz Conservatory with Ludovica von Kaan. He was largely self-taught after age 16, gave his first public recital at 17 in Graz, and won the Busoni Competition prize at 18, launching his career.
family_context_summary: Born to a non-musical family in Vizmberk, Czechoslovakia. Father worked as an architectural engineer, businessman, resort hotel manager, and cinema director. The family moved frequently between Yugoslavia and Austria. There was no music in the household.
parent_family_domain_summary: No musical family background. Father had various non-musical professions. Brendel explicitly stated he was not a child prodigy and his parents were not musicians.
milestone_by_age_26: Won fourth prize at the Ferruccio Busoni Piano Competition in 1949 at age 18, made his first recording (Prokofiev Piano Concerto No. 5) in 1950 at 19, and made the world premiere recording of Liszt's Weihnachtsbaum in 1952 at 21, establishing an international performing and recording career.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Graz Conservatory, Busoni Competition, self-taught after 16, early recordings, Edwin Fischer master classes, wartime displacement

name: Gastone Nencini
evidence_summary: Nencini came from a wealthy family of cattle merchants in Tuscany, though his father disapproved of his cycling ambitions. His early advantage was primarily geographic, growing up in the heartland of Italian cycling, and physical, as he was a gifted descender and powerful all-rounder. He joined the strongest amateur team in Tuscany and progressed rapidly, winning silver at the 1953 World Championships amateur road race before turning professional. No evidence of parental cycling domain expertise or inherited networks was found in reviewed sources.
early_history_summary: Nencini grew up in a wealthy family of cattle merchants in Barberino di Mugello, Tuscany, and began cycling at age eighteen after playing football as a goalkeeper. He joined the strongest amateur team in Tuscany, S.S. Oltrarno, in 1950 and quickly established himself as a promising climber and descender. He won silver at the 1953 World Championships amateur road race and turned professional that same year with Legnano-Pirelli.
family_context_summary: Born to a wealthy family of cattle merchants in Barberino di Mugello, Tuscany; father Attilio was a well-known cattle merchant who disapproved of his cycling ambitions.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; father was a cattle merchant with no known connection to cycling.
milestone_by_age_26: Won silver at the 1953 World Championships amateur road race and turned professional with Legnano-Pirelli at age 23; won the Giro d'Italia mountains classification and individual stages in 1955 at age 25.

name: Rafael Osuna
evidence_summary: Osuna's early athletic talent was evident in table tennis, where he won Mexico's national open championship before age 10. His transition to tennis was facilitated by a full scholarship to USC under legendary coach George Toley, who identified his raw athleticism and retaught him proper technique. His doubles partnership with Dennis Ralston at USC proved catalytic, as the pair won Wimbledon in 1960 before playing a single college match. No family background information was found in reviewed sources, making it difficult to assess inherited advantages.
early_history_summary: Osuna won Mexico's national table tennis championship before age 10, then transitioned to tennis after receiving a full scholarship to USC from coach George Toley, who retaught him proper technique. He won the Wimbledon men's doubles with Dennis Ralston in 1960 at age 21, before either had played a college match, and went on to win the US Championships singles title in 1963 at age 25, reaching world No. 1.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources.

name: Kipchoge Keino
evidence_summary: Keino's early life was marked by adversity: he was orphaned young and raised by an aunt in Kenya's Rift Valley, herding goats and running in high-altitude terrain that naturally built endurance. His father was noted as a long-distance runner who encouraged him, though details are sparse. He joined the Kenya Police, which provided a structured athletic platform, and emerged as a world-class runner in his early twenties. His 1965 world records in the 3000m and 5000m at age 25 were the product of natural high-altitude conditioning, self-driven training, and the rising wave of Kenyan distance running.
early_history_summary: Keino grew up orphaned in Kenya's Rift Valley, herding goats and running in the high-altitude hill country. He joined the Kenya Police and began his international running career at the 1962 Commonwealth Games. In 1965 at age 25, he broke both the 3000m and 5000m world records, and in 1966, he won gold in both the mile and 3-miles at the Commonwealth Games.
family_context_summary: Born in Kipsamo, Nandi District, Kenya; parents died when he was young and he was raised by an aunt; herded goats as a child.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a long-distance runner who encouraged his son in the sport, according to Britannica.
milestone_by_age_26: Broke the 3000m and 5000m world records in 1965 at age 25, and won gold in both the mile and 3-miles at the 1966 Commonwealth Games at age 26.

name: Henryk Górecki
evidence_summary: Górecki grew up in modest circumstances in rural Silesia, losing his pianist mother at age two and being discouraged from music by his father and stepmother. He persisted, beginning violin lessons at 10, teaching school to support himself, and studying at the Academy of Music in Katowice under Bolesław Szabelski. The post-Stalin cultural thaw of 1956 opened opportunities for avant-garde exploration, and by 1958 he had a monographic concert at the Silesian State Philharmonic and debuted at the Warsaw Autumn Festival, establishing himself as a leading Polish avant-garde composer by his mid-20s.
early_history_summary: Górecki was born in a small Silesian village to a railway worker father and a pianist mother who died when he was two. Despite being discouraged from music, he began violin lessons at age 10. He taught school from 1951-53, then studied at the State Higher School of Music in Katowice from 1955-60 under Bolesław Szabelski. His first public performances in 1958 led to a Warsaw Autumn Festival debut and international recognition.
family_context_summary: Born to Roman Górecki, a railway station worker and amateur musician, and Otylia, a pianist who died when Henryk was two years old. The family lived modestly in rural Silesia. His father and stepmother discouraged his musical interests.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother played piano but died when he was two; father was an amateur musician who worked at a railway station. No professional music domain transfer documented due to early mother's death and family discouragement.
milestone_by_age_26: Had a monographic concert devoted entirely to his music at the Silesian State Philharmonic in Katowice in February 1958 at age 24, and completed his First Symphony in 1959 at age 25, marking his arrival as a leading figure of the Polish avant-garde.
primary_early_advantage_tags: orphaned mother, rural poverty, self-taught beginnings, Polish cultural thaw, Warsaw Autumn Festival, mentor Szabelski

name: Alberto Tomba
evidence_summary: Tomba's path was shaped by his wealthy textile-merchant father who loved skiing and arranged for a former national team skier, Roberto Siorpaes, to coach Alberto from age 7. He trained intensively in Cortina d'Ampezzo, skied competitively from his early teens, and benefited from the Italian alpine skiing pipeline. His natural physical talent and power (182cm, 90kg) suited the new spring-loaded ski gates. By 21 he had won two Olympic golds, making him one of the greatest Alpine skiers in history.
early_history_summary: Born to a wealthy Bolognese textile merchant, Tomba started skiing at age 7 under special teacher Roberto Siorpaes, a former national team skier, arranged by his father. He showed natural talent early, skied competitively through his teens, made his World Cup debut at 18 in 1985, and burst onto the scene with his first World Cup victory in November 1987 followed by double Olympic gold at Calgary in 1988.
family_context_summary: Son of Franco Tomba, a wealthy Bolognese textile industry businessman who was a keen skier and arranged for special coaching from age 7. The family's wealth enabled access to training in Cortina d'Ampezzo and dedicated coaching.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Franco was a keen skier since attending college in Switzerland and procured a special teacher, Roberto Siorpaes, a former national team slalom skier, to train Alberto from age 7.
milestone_by_age_26: Won two Olympic gold medals (giant slalom and slalom) at the 1988 Calgary Winter Olympics at age 21, after securing his first World Cup victory in November 1987.
primary_early_advantage_tags: wealthy family, dedicated coach from age 7, Cortina d'Ampezzo training, Italian skiing pipeline, early talent

early_history_summary: Born in Andermatt, a Swiss alpine village, Russi grew up immersed in skiing and joined the SC Gotthard Andermatt club. name: Jarno Saarinen
evidence_summary: Saarinen's path was largely self-created: he apprenticed at a motorcycle factory at 15, developed unique ice-racing techniques in Finland, and funded his early GP career by borrowing from four banks. His mechanical engineering education gave him a technical edge in bike setup. The Finnish ice racing culture provided a distinctive training ground, but his success came from self-directed repetition and innovation rather than inherited advantages. By 25, he was a world championship podium finisher and GP winner.
early_history_summary: Born in Turku, Finland, Saarinen began racing at age 16 in ice races. At 15, he became an apprentice and test-rider at the Tunturi-Puch motorcycle factory. He won the 250cc Finnish ice racing national championship in 1965 at age 20, and the 125cc and 250cc Finnish road racing national championships in 1969 at age 24. He made his Grand Prix debut in 1968 and competed in his first full world championship season in 1970, finishing 4th in the 250cc class. He studied mechanical engineering at university while racing, graduating with top marks in 1971.
family_context_summary: Born in Turku, Finland; his family had operated a funeral home business since 1902. He had two older brothers and one younger brother, all of whom raced motorcycles at some point. The family was not wealthy enough to fund his racing, which was financially stressful.
parent_family_domain_summary: No direct family domain advantage in motorcycle racing, though the family's entrepreneurial background (funeral home) may have provided a business-oriented mindset. His brothers also raced motorcycles, suggesting a family culture of motorcycling.
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first Grand Prix race in Czechoslovakia in 1971 and finished 2nd in the 350cc world championship and 3rd in the 250cc world championship at age 25, establishing himself as one of the most promising motorcycle racers of his era.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Tunturi-Puch apprenticeship, ice racing technique, self-funded, mechanical engineering, Finnish racing culture

name: Khaby Lame
evidence_summary: Khaby Lame's rise was catalyzed by constraint: a laid-off factory worker in public housing during COVID-19, he turned to TikTok with no prior content creation experience, no family resources, and no media connections. The TikTok platform provided massive native distribution, and the COVID pandemic created a structural wave of platform growth. His natural comedic presence and expressive face enabled a distinctive silent comedy format that resonated globally. No inherited advantages are documented; his success was entirely self-created from adversity.
early_history_summary: Born in Dakar, Senegal, Lame moved to Italy with his family at age one and grew up in a public housing complex in Chivasso, near Turin. He worked as a CNC machine operator at a factory before being laid off in March 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. He began posting TikTok videos—initially dancing and watching video games—before developing his signature silent comedy format of reacting to overly complicated life hacks with simple solutions. His follower count exploded, reaching 100 million by early 2022 and surpassing Charli D'Amelio as the most-followed TikToker in April 2022.
family_context_summary: Born in Dakar, Senegal to a working-class family that moved to Italy when he was one year old. He grew up in a public housing complex in Chivasso, near Turin. His father was on layoffs and his mother was a housewife. He worked various odd jobs including bricklayer, window cleaner, Amazon worker, and kitchen assistant before becoming a CNC machine operator.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family domain advantage in media or entertainment. Parents were working-class immigrants with no media connections.
milestone_by_age_26: Became the most-followed person on TikTok in April 2022 at age 22 with 142 million followers, surpassing Charli D'Amelio, after starting to post videos in March 2020 following a factory layoff.
primary_early_advantage_tags: COVID layoff, TikTok platform, immigrant background, public housing, silent comedy

name: Buvaisar Saitiev

Despite losing his bricklayer father at 13 and being raised by a single mother with six children, the regional wrestling ecosystem and state sports pipeline provided world-class training. His younger brother Adam also became an Olympic champion, reflecting both family talent and the elite training environment. By 20, Saitiev was a world champion; by 21, an Olympic champion.
early_history_summary: Born in Khasavyurt, Dagestan to a Chechen family, Saitiev started wrestling at age 6-8 at a local sports school. His father, a bricklayer, died in a car accident when Saitiev was 13, leaving his mother to raise six children. He achieved the master of sport qualification at 14 and moved to Novokuznetsk at 15 to a sports boarding school. In 1992 at age 17, he moved to Krasnoyarsk to train at the prestigious wrestling center under legendary coach Dmitri Mindiashvili. He won his first World Championship gold in 1995 at 20 and Olympic gold in 1996 at 21.
family_context_summary: Born in Khasavyurt, Dagestan to a Chechen family. Father was a bricklayer who died in a car accident in 1988 when Saitiev was 13. Mother was a housewife who raised six children (four sons and two daughters) alone after the father's death. The family was not wealthy, and the children were immersed in the regional wrestling culture.
parent_family_domain_summary: No parental domain advantage in wrestling. Father was a bricklayer; mother was a housewife. However, the Dagestan/Chechnya region has a deep wrestling culture, and Saitiev's younger brother Adam also became an Olympic champion wrestler, suggesting a family culture that valued wrestling.
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first World Championship gold medal in 1995 at age 20 and Olympic gold medal at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics at age 21, establishing himself as the dominant freestyle wrestler of his era with multiple world and European titles by 26.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Krasnoyarsk wrestling center, Mindiashvili coaching, Dagestan wrestling culture, early specialization, brother Adam

name: Assar Rönnlund
evidence_summary: Assar Rönnlund grew up in a small logging village in northern Sweden, the son of a lumberjack, and worked as a timberman at 15. This rural Nordic environment provided deep immersion in cross-country skiing culture and terrain. He broke through at the 1959 Swedish Championships and won two golds and a silver at the 1962 World Championships at age 26, earning Sweden's top sports honor. His path was defined by geographic immersion in a skiing frontier and physical labor from a young age rather than inherited advantages.
early_history_summary: Born in Sävar near Umeå, Sweden, Rönnlund grew up in the small village of Ytterträsk. His father was a lumberjack, and at 15 Assar worked in the forest as a timberman. He broke through at the 1959 Swedish Championships, winning gold in the 30 km ahead of favorite Sixten Jernberg. He competed at the 1960 Olympics (12th in 50 km) before his dominant 1962 World Championships performance.
family_context_summary: Father was a lumberjack in the small village of Ytterträsk in Sävar municipality, northern Sweden. Assar worked as a timberman at age 15. The family was working-class in a rural Nordic setting.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of parental skiing expertise, but growing up in rural northern Sweden provided natural proximity to cross-country skiing culture and terrain.
milestone_by_age_26: Won two gold medals (15 km and 4×10 km relay) and a silver (50 km) at the 1962 FIS Nordic World Ski Championships in Zakopane at age 26, earning the Svenska Dagbladet Gold Medal as Sweden's best sports feat of the year.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Nordic skiing culture, rural forest upbringing, IFK Umeå club, early physical labor

name: Egon Zimmermann
evidence_summary: Zimmermann's key advantage was growing up in Lech am Arlberg as it transformed into a world-class ski resort, providing daily access to the mountains and an emerging alpine skiing culture. Despite post-war poverty and fourth-hand skis, the geographic immersion in Austria's skiing frontier compensated for lack of formal training. His promotion to the national team at 18 gave him access to elite coaching and competition. The adversity of his interrupted development (forced chef apprenticeship) may have created urgency when he returned to skiing.
early_history_summary: Zimmermann was raised on a farm near Lech, Vorarlberg, Austria, which blossomed into a ski resort during his childhood. His family converted their farmhouse into a pension. Despite post-war poverty and having no formal training, he won a clean sweep of the 1958 Junior Championships at age 19 after returning from a forced chef apprenticeship in Paris. He was promoted to the Austrian national team and won World Championship medals at 23.
family_context_summary: Raised on a farm near Lech, Vorarlberg, Austria, during post-World War II poverty. His family converted their farmhouse into a pension as Lech developed into a ski resort. His father forced him into a chef apprenticeship in Paris at 15, interrupting his skiing development.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; the family ran a farm and later a pension in a growing ski resort town, providing geographic proximity to skiing but not direct domain expertise.
milestone_by_age_26: Won gold in giant slalom and bronze in downhill at the 1962 World Championships in Chamonix at age 23, was named European 'Skier of the Year' in 1963, and won Olympic gold in the downhill at the 1964 Innsbruck Winter Olympics at age 25, appearing on the cover of Sports Illustrated.

evidence_summary: Wikipedia, DoomWiki, and Masters of Doom-aligned secondary sources confirm birth May 5, 1969, Softdisk origins, id founding February 1991 (age 21), and art leadership on Wolfenstein 3D and Doom before age 25.
